hypotheses.title: FunctionQualifiersFrom rebuilds a fresh qualifier list semtype on every function type, although only 4 values exist, defeating identity fast paths in function subtype checks
hypotheses.issue: semtypes/function_qualifiers.go: FunctionQualifiersFrom -> createSemType runs NewListDefinition().Define(env, {isolatedTy, transactionalTy}) on every call, yet (isolated, transactional) only has 4 possible values. Each call allocates fresh cell atoms and a list atom (env.cellAtom/env.listAtom insert into env.atomTable under atomTableMutex; the table is keyed by AtomicType pointer identity so nothing is deduplicated and it grows without bound) and interns new BDD nodes (~1.85us, 13 allocs, 2 new atoms per call). It is called for every function type built: opaque.FunctionSemType via type_resolver.typeFromFunctionSignature (every lambda in resolveInferredLambdaFunctionExpr, every monomorphizeDependentCall, method member types), plus direct calls in type_resolver.go, semtypes core.go/listener.go/stream_member.go and desugar. The larger cost is downstream: because every function atom carries its own unique qualifiers BDD, semtypes/function_ops.go functionPathIsEmpty (IsSubtype(cx, qualifiers, t2)) and functionUnionQualifiers can never hit the b1 == b2 identity shortcut in bddDiff nor the emptiness memo, so every function subtype check (lambda vs expected function type, IsSubtype(fn, isolated fn), call-argument validation) performs a full list-emptiness check on freshly built BDDs. On corpus/bench/10-bench/expressions-v.bal ~6% of CPU samples were in functionPathIsEmpty.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a .bal file with many function-typed values (lambdas, function
references) so stage-5 builds many function semtypes and runs function
subtype checks.  Usage: gen_fnq.py <num_funcs> <lambdas_per_func>"""
import sys
nf = int(sys.argv[1]); per = int(sys.argv[2])
o = ["import ballerina/io;", "",
     "function apply(function (int) returns int g, int v) returns int => g(v);",
     "isolated function applyIso(isolated function (int) returns int g, int v) returns int => g(v);",
     "function inc(int x) returns int => x + 1;", ""]
for f in range(nf):
    o.append(f"function f{f}(int s) returns int {{")
    o.append("    int acc = s;")
    for i in range(per):
        k = i % 4
        if k == 0:
            o.append(f"    acc = apply(x => x + {i}, acc);")
        elif k == 1:
            o.append(f"    function (int) returns int h{i} = function(int y) returns int {{ return y - {i}; }};")
            o.append(f"    acc = h{i}(acc);")
        elif k == 2:
            o.append(f"    acc = applyIso(z => z * 1, acc);")
        else:
            o.append(f"    function (int) returns int r{i} = inc;")
            o.append(f"    acc = apply(r{i}, acc) - 1;")
    o.append("    return acc;")
    o.append("}")
o.append("public function main() {")
o.append("    int t = 0;")
for f in range(nf):
    o.append(f"    t += f{f}({f});")
o.append("    io:println(t);")
o.append("}")
print("\n".join(o))
reproducer.command: python3 gen_fnq.py 500 40 > fnq.bal && ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> fnq.bal  (also: hyperfine -w 1 -r 8 -N 'bal run fnq.bal'; bal run --stats fnq.bal and read the fnq Analysis lines)

hypotheses.fix_approach: Precompute the 4 qualifier SemTypes once per env in newPreallocatedTypeVals (called from CreateTypeEnv, the only env constructor, before the env is shared) as a [2][2]SemType indexed by [isolated][transactional], and have FunctionQualifiersFrom return the cached value. The cache is immutable after construction so concurrent module analysis needs no locking. Pitfalls: the qualifiers must be built after the basic cell type vals are assigned to env.preallocatedTypeVals (createSemType needs them) and nothing in the remaining preallocation builders (json/anydata/cloneable/ordered) may call FunctionQualifiersFrom before the cache is filled. Cached atoms are permanent (created before Freeze), so post-freeze calls also stop creating ephemeral atoms under ephemeralMu. Verification: make test passed; make test-race reported zero data races but one timing-sensitive runtime lib test (lib/subset3/task-misfire1-v.bal) failed once under race slowdown and passed 3/3 when rerun in isolation (unrelated to the change).

notes: Side observation (not measured in isolation): semantics/internal/types/type_resolver.go monomorphizeDependentCall builds a fresh monomorphized symbol, signature and function type for every call to a dependently-typed function (e.g. cloneWithType) even with identical argument types; ~18% of CPU on a 40k-call probe file. Candidate for a future hunt.
